Provenance is a capture problem before it is a ledger problem
blocks.sub: Source-signed events, identity crosswalks and drilled recalls over ledger choice

blocks.x: Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust is delivered by an Achala practice team that stays through industrialization. Achala runs permissioned networks where every participant sees the same truth and no one can change it alone. Consensus rules, key ceremonies and inspection exports are documented from day one — shared trust that survives an audit. Who this is for: CFOs and operations heads reconciling across organizations, and the regulators who demand inspection views.

The measure that matters is the recall drill: given a batch, how fast can you enumerate everything that touched it, forward and backward, with evidence attached? Minutes is the target; weeks is the industry norm.
Below: the failure modes that make provenance decorative, the reference architecture of the capture chain, and the console that drills recalls.

stages.name: Trigger
stages.detail: The recall trigger classifies scope (lot, date range, facility) from the suspect event; scope proposal is generated from the trail, not from memory.

stages.name: Reconstruct
stages.detail: Distribution reconstruction walks the anchored trail to store level with quantities; the reconstruction artifact is what the regulator receives.

stages.name: Notify
stages.detail: Notification duties execute by jurisdiction and contract; the duty chain is pre-mapped so notifications run in parallel, not in sequence.

stages.name: Disposition
stages.detail: Unit-level disposition (quarantine, return, destroy) recorded with actor binding; the ledger anchors the record so the disposition survives the dispute.

stages.name: Debrief
stages.detail: Post-drill gaps feed the capture-investment list: weak-attestation hops get device binding next quarter — the drill is the roadmap's source.

widgets.note: Recalls are rehearsed quarterly with real scope generation — the drill results are the readiness evidence auditors ask for first.

Capture fidelity beats ledger choice
blocks.sub: The capture chain, the identity crosswalk and recall drills, what actually makes provenance defensible

blocks.x: Provenance programs decorate supply chains when the events are typed into portals at the end of the week; they defend supply chains when capture happens at the source, signed by the device or system that observed the physical event. The capture chain therefore runs from scanners, IoT signals and ERP events through a normalization layer that anchors batches as merkle roots, the full chain is reconstructable from the roots plus the sealed evidence store, and the identity crosswalk maps EPCIS identifiers to real parties so 'lot 4711' has a name, a site and a certification status behind it.

Recall drills are the product test: on a schedule, the reconstruction service must rebuild the affected lot's journey, forward and backward trace, inside the drill window, with the evidence pack a regulator expects. Partner onboarding is evidence-gated (a partner joins with capture capability proven on their line, not with a signed promise), and capture coverage is measured per tier, because tier-2 and tier-3 blindness is where recalls quietly fail.

items: Events signed by devices and systems that observed them, not retyped later.
Merkle roots on-ledger; the full chain reconstructs from roots plus sealed evidence.
Every EPCIS identifier resolves to a party, site and certification status.
Forward and backward trace rehearsed to a clock, with regulator-grade packs.
Why is provenance a capture problem before a ledger problem?

A ledger anchors what reaches it; if handoff events never get captured, the trail is decorative. Coverage per partner tier is the design target, the console shows the honest weak points, and onboarding gates prove capture before a partner ships.
How does this survive a real recall drill?

Drills are the release evidence: a batch recall reconstructs the chain in minutes, lists affected lots and downstream recipients, and produces the regulator-ready report. The console headline is recall time for exactly this reason.
What about partners with no digital systems?

The defaults table covers capture per partner class, label scans, mobile capture or EDI. Coverage targets are signed per class, and deviations where a partner cannot meet capture are priced and logged, not papered over.
Can we anchor our existing certificates and documents?
Yes, document hashes anchor at the event where the certificate is produced, so provenance covers the paper trail as well as the goods. The evidence plane reconciles both.
Which ledger do you use — and does it matter?

Capture fidelity beats ledger choice: the architecture is ledger-agnostic, chosen against your partner network and regulator expectations. The gates prove the capture chain; the ledger is a decision, not a default.
